 Canva announces layoffs, job changes for about 22% of workforce 
 November 4, 2026 | 6:21 pm 
 CANVA.COM 
 CANVA, INC. announced job cuts and a sweeping overhaul that will impact more than one-fifth of the workforce, as artificial intelligence (AI) forces a structural reckoning at one of Australia’s highest-profile technology companies. 
 Some 1,271 people, or 22% of Canva’s staff, will lose their jobs, change roles or relocate to central hubs, Chief Executive Of fi cer Melanie Perkins said in a note to employees that was posted on the fi rm’s website on Wednesday.
 The sweeping changes at Canva, an online design and publishing platform, mirror the broader upheaval across the software industry. Investors have wiped billions of dollars from the value of these fi rms amid concerns new technology like Anthropic PBC’s Claude will cannibalize their business.
 Arti fi cial intelligence is allowing people to do more on their own without specialty programs, while companies are using AI to operate with fewer workers.
 “New technology is transforming what people can create, how they create it, and what they expect from the products they use,” Ms. Perkins wrote in the note. “I’ve come to the dif fi cult conclusion that small changes won’t be enough.”
 Ms. Perkins, who co-founded Canva with Cliff Obrecht and Cameron Adams, didn’t specify how many staff would lose their jobs. But after the Sydney-based fi rm’s growth slowed for the fi rst time in a decade, Ms. Perkins said Canva needs to become a simpler business and return to running small, empowered teams. There will be fewer niche specializations, she said. 
 She described the reorganization as “the hardest moment in our 13-year history.”
 Sydney will become the main base for more of Canva’s product teams. Ms. Perkins said more people will work face-to-face, and most hybrid staff will spend two to three days in the of fi ce a week from January.
 Canva has been preparing for a potential listing, and the overhaul leaves the company in a delicate fi nancial balance. After hitting a $40 billion high in 2021, Canva’s valuation tumbled to roughly $26 billion a year later during a broad tech selloff. While Canva’s dollar worth subsequently rebounded, the effect of more recent tumult is not yet clear.
 While the AI era has led to widespread job losses, investors are also questioning when, or even if, the vast associated investments will deliver a fi nancial dividend.
 Firmus Grid Ltd. last month scrapped a planned Australian initial public offering of up to $5.5 billion, turning a rising star of the AI data center boom into one of the biggest deal flops in recent memory. Nextdc Ltd. shares plummeted in October after the data center operator said it was considering force majeure options and cut earnings guidance. — Bloomberg
